provisions.summary: Sets standard deduction at the 2023 amounts ($4,400 single, $6,424 head of household, $8,800 joint) with the doubled amounts below an AGI cap, and repeals the scheduled step-ups to $8,000/$12,000/$16,000 and beyond. Modeled as flat amounts for all years; the AGI test is not expressible
provisions.approximation: The bill's amounts apply only to returns with AGI under $100,000 (joint under $200,000), and the bill does not say what applies above those limits. The spec applies the amounts to every return, so higher-income filers keep a deduction the bill may deny them and the revenue estimate is likely too low (the cost too high). The repealed step-ups are in effect removed, so the amounts are well below current law's $8,000/$12,000/$16,000 for 2027.
provisions.quote: $2,200 or $4,400 for a return with an adjusted gross income less than $100,000, in the case of an individual who is not married

notes: Section 12 sets one schedule for tax years after Dec 31, 2025 and repeals the later scheduled vintages, so a single vintage from 2027 holds through 2031. The 2026 year is outside the modeled range. The first bracket's rate is the bill's '0% of taxable income', written as 0 in the spec. Part VIII (Maui fund) takes effect July 1, 2025; the rest applies to taxable years after Dec 31, 2024. Section 10 lists the standard deduction amounts for 'a return with an adjusted gross income of less than $200,000' (joint) and $100,000 (others), and the bill's text is silent above those limits. The bill describes the amounts as 'doubled' but the stated figures equal the 2023 base amounts, so the doubling is not expressed in the text. Section 12 retains the 11% top rate at $400,000 (joint), $300,000 (head of household) and $200,000 (single). Credits (eitc_percent, food_excise) are untouched by the bill; Act 163's expansions end after 2027 under current law and the bill does not extend them. The general excise rate steps (sections 3, 5, 6) have blank rates, so no revenue estimate can be made for the excise change even though the exemptions in section 2 would reduce revenue. Section 7's cross-reference to 'Act , Session Laws of Hawaii 2025' is also blank.
